text:
Ava L.: Hey all — launching Community Runbooks & Playbooks v1 :tada: 
Ava L.: This repo bundles ops/runbook templates, incident playbooks, integration checklists, and a contrib guide for maintainers. Goal: make onboarding and incident responses repeatable across community projects.
Ava L.: Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/community-runbooks (release v1.0.0)
Ava L.: Quick install snippet in case folks want the CLI helpers:```bash
pip install redwood-runbooks==1.0.0
# or
git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/community-runbooks && cd community-runbooks
```
Ava L.: TL;DR: templates for runbooks, runbook-lint, playbook examples (deploy, rollback, security incident), and a CONTRIBUTING.md with rotation suggestions.
community-bot: release published: community-runbooks@v1.0.0 — changelog: "initial runbooks + linter + templates" — artifacts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/community-runbooks/releases/tag/v1.0.0
Priya: love this. :heart_eyes: Is there a recommended cadence for runbook reviews? weekly/monthly?
Ava L.: Great q — default recommendation in CONTRIBUTING is quarterly reviews for critical runbooks, monthly for active integrations. We also included a short checklist for reviewers.
Derek: I can run the first review for the deploy/rollback playbook next week. Putting it on my calendar. :ok_hand:
Sam: Nice work. Quick Q: does this repo require a CLA or special contributor agreement for maintainers?
ops-bot: Note: repo flagged for CLA check — maintainers should enable the CLA bot or follow the CONTRIBUTING checklist to add the CLA label. See docs/cla.md
Ava L.: We kept it permissive but added an optional CLA flow in docs/cla.md. For enterprise maintainers who want tighter controls, we listed recommended GitHub apps (CLA, DCO) in the ops appendix.
Priya: Can we add a short workshop / office hours to walk contributors through the runbook-lint and the playbook examples? Might help adoption.
Ava L.: Yes — scheduling a 60-min office hours session next Wednesday 11am PT. Signup: https://cal.com/redwood/community-runbooks-officehrs — will post calendar invite.
Derek: Also, I noticed a placeholder in security-incident.md about PSP tokens. I'll open a tiny PR to clarify and add a test snippet.
Sam: If someone wants to include localization or translated runbooks, where would that live?
Ava L.: We added i18n guidelines in docs/i18n.md — translations go under /i18n/<lang>/ with a short metadata header. Priya, maybe you or volunteers can coordinate initial translations for en-US and fr-FR?
Priya: happy to coordinate volunteer translators. I'll spin up a short issue and tag folks.
community-bot: Notice: onboarding checklist created for new maintainers — /docs/maintainers-onboarding.md
Ava L.: Thanks team. If you notice anything missing or want a different template (e.g., PCI/PHI specific playbook), open an issue and tag @Ava L. We'll prioritize based on demand. :sparkles: 
Sam: Congrats on the launch — looks very polished. :tada:
Ava L.: Appreciate it! Will follow up with a short post in the community forum and newsletter this afternoon.
ops-bot: Reminder: for any changes to CI or deploy steps, open a PR and add the label "infra-impact" so SRE gets a heads-up.
Derek: PR for security-incident.md opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/community-runbooks/pull/12 — small wording + test snippet.
Priya: I'll take the translations issue once it's up. :raised_hands:
Ava L.: Wonderful. Closing notes: v1 is intentionally minimal — we expect iterative contributions. Big thanks to the folks who helped — @Derek @Priya @Sam and everyone who reviewed. :heart:
